protocol.freeze_rule: calibration uses 2010 weeks only; priors cite work published before February 2013; specification chosen on 2010 pseudo-changes

no_change.label: No change
no_change.description: No change keeps each group at its 2010 average and its quits at the 2010 exit rate of staff (17.3% over 38 weeks); working at home changes nothing.

seasonal.label: Same weeks last year
seasonal.description: Same weeks last year moves each group's 2010 average by how all staff's output in the same weeks of 2010 differed from the end of 2010; no effect of working at home.

trend.label: Recent trend
trend.description: Recent trend extends a straight line through each group's 2010 weekly averages over the experiment weeks.

literature.label: Earlier research
literature.description: Earlier research applies a 2007 meta-analysis of 46 telecommuting studies directly: supervisor-rated or objective performance +0.36 standard deviations and turnover intent -0.17 standard deviations, carried to quits through the intent-to-quit correlation of 0.38 from a 2000 turnover meta-analysis. Both groups start from their 2010 averages.

d_perf.source: Telecommuting and supervisor-rated or objective job performance: mean r = .18, d = .36, 95% CI for r .09 to .26 (k = 4, n = 484); Gajendran & Harrison (2007), 'The good, the bad, and the unknown about telecommuting', Journal of Applied Psychology 92(6), 1524-1541, Table 1. The range converts the CI for r to d (2r / sqrt(1 - r^2)). Applied as a shift of d between-person standard deviations of each measure.

d_turnover_intent.source: Telecommuting and turnover intent: mean r = -.08, d = -.17, 95% CI for r -.11 to -.06 (k = 9, n = 7,580); Gajendran & Harrison (2007), Table 1. Range converts the CI to d.

rho_intent_quit.source: Quit intentions predict actual turnover: corrected r = .38 (uncorrected .35, second correction .45; k = 71, N = 63,232); Griffeth, Hom & Gaertner (2000), 'A meta-analysis of antecedents and correlates of employee turnover', Journal of Management 26(3), 463-488. Used as the shift in the latent quit liability per SD of intent.

rho_tenure_quit.source: Organisational tenure and turnover: r = -.20 (corrected -.20 and -.23; 1995 estimate -.17); Griffeth, Hom & Gaertner (2000). Latent quit liability per SD of tenure within the twins.

rho_age_quit.source: Age and turnover: r = -.09 (corrected -.09 and -.11; 1995 estimate -.12); Griffeth, Hom & Gaertner (2000). Latent quit liability per SD of age within the twins.

intensity_share_2d.source: Effect of two home days relative to four (used only by the two-day alternative). Gajendran & Harrison (2007), Table 3: telecommuting lowered work-family conflict at high intensity (2.5 or more days, r = -.16) about three times as much as at low intensity (r = -.05), while its link with perceived autonomy did not differ by intensity (r = .16 vs .15). The range spans those two ratios; the central value is their midpoint.

reference_source: Bloom, Liang, Roberts & Ying (2015) replication files (authors' copy; Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/PZQOB1); computed by instances/ctrip/ingest/run.py
